title: JAMB Science
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public JAMB UTME science-subject syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: The old bridge had been weakened by years of flood water, yet the traders kept crossing it because the only alternative was a two-hour detour. When it finally collapsed, no one was surprised. Why did the traders continue to use the bridge?
options: The detour was far too long to be convenient
They had no idea that the bridge was weak
They secretly wanted the bridge to collapse
The bridge had been rebuilt the previous week
items.explanation: The passage states the only alternative was a two-hour detour, so traders accepted the risk for convenience. The other options add facts the passage never mentions and even contradict it.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: The manager's reply was terse, and the workers understood at once that he had no time for long explanations. Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word terse.
items.explanation: Terse means using very few words while still being clear, so brief and to the point fits best. Angry, vague and friendly describe tone or length but not the economy of words that terse denotes.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: The witness gave a candid account of the incident and did not hide anything. Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word candid.
items.explanation: Candid means open and truthful, so its opposite is evasive, meaning deliberately unclear. Honest is a synonym, while lengthy and written describe form rather than truthfulness.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Neither the teacher nor the students ...... present when the bell rang for assembly. Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
items.explanation: With neither-nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, which is students, a plural, so were is correct. Was and is are singular, and be cannot stand as the finite verb here.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: The principal insisted ...... the pupils wearing their complete uniforms throughout the school term. Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
items.explanation: The verb insist is followed by the preposition on when it takes a noun or gerund. For, at and with do not form the standard collocation insist on.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: When the chairman said the new project would gulp a lot of money, he meant that the project would
options: consume a great deal of funds
items.explanation: To gulp money is an idiom meaning to swallow or consume large amounts of it. The other options describe failure, investment or speed and miss the idea of heavy spending.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: In the sentence the swift runner overtook all his rivals, the word swift functions as
items.explanation: Swift describes the noun runner, so it is an adjective. An adverb would modify a verb, a noun would name something, and a verb would show action or state.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Choose the option whose first sound is different from the first sound of the other three words.
items.explanation: In kettle the k is pronounced, while in knife, knee and knight the initial k is silent and the words begin with the n sound.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Adaeze read the telegram twice and then sat down quietly staring at the wall, although that morning she had been laughing with her friends. The passage suggests that the telegram
options: was a bill she had expected
had been written by her friends
items.explanation: Her sudden silence after laughter implies the message upset her, so it brought sad news. The other options do not explain the change in her mood.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: The government promised to ...... the suffering of the flood victims by supplying relief materials quickly. Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
items.explanation: To alleviate means to make suffering less severe, which matches the supply of relief. Aggravate, prolong and multiply would all increase the suffering rather than ease it.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Chidi was widely praised for his generosity toward the poor. Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word generosity.
items.explanation: Generosity is the habit of giving freely, so its opposite is stinginess, the refusal to give. Kindness and charity are close in meaning, and wealth is an unrelated noun.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: Choose the option that is the correct plural form of the word crisis.
items.explanation: Nouns ending in -is form the plural by changing -is to -es, giving crises. Adding -s or leaving the word unchanged are both incorrect for this class of nouns.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: One of the boys ...... absent from school yesterday without any reason. Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
items.explanation: The true subject is one, which is singular, so the singular past verb was is required. Were, are and have been are plural or present forms that do not agree.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: For decades the village relied on rain-fed farming, but when the rains became unreliable the farmers dug boreholes and planted drought-resistant crops, so that their harvests, though smaller, no longer failed completely. What is the main idea of the passage?
options: The farmers gave up farming when the rains failed
The farmers adapted their methods to cope with unreliable rainfall
Rain-fed farming is always more dependable than irrigation
The boreholes caused the rains to return to the village
items.explanation: The passage describes farmers changing their practices to survive unreliable rain, so adaptation is the central idea. The other options contradict the passage or introduce claims it does not make.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: The doctor advised the patient to ...... smoking at once in order to protect his lungs. Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
items.explanation: To give up means to stop a habit, so give up smoking is correct. Give in means to surrender, and give off or give out mean to emit or distribute, which do not fit the sentence.
items.reference: JAMB UTME Syllabus - Use of English

items.stem: A body of mass 5 kg is accelerated uniformly from rest to a speed of 20 m/s in 4 seconds. Calculate the net force acting on the body.
items.explanation: Acceleration is 20 divided by 4, which is 5 m/s^2, and force is mass times acceleration, so 5 kg times 5 m/s^2 gives 25 N. The other values misuse the figures.

items.stem: A car covers 60 km in the first hour and 90 km in the next two hours. Calculate the average speed of the car for the whole journey.
items.explanation: Average speed is total distance over total time, so 150 km divided by 3 hours gives 50 km/h. The others use only part of the journey or divide incorrectly.

items.stem: Which of the following is the SI unit of electric current?
items.explanation: The ampere is the SI base unit of current. The volt measures potential difference, the coulomb measures charge, and the ohm measures resistance.

items.stem: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of 30 degrees. Calculate the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray.
items.explanation: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence at 30 degrees, so the angle between the two rays is 180 minus twice 30, that is 120 degrees. The others confuse this with the glancing angle.

items.stem: A body moving with a velocity of 10 m/s is brought to rest in 2 seconds. Calculate the magnitude of its deceleration.
items.explanation: Deceleration is the change in velocity over time, so 10 m/s divided by 2 s gives 5 m/s^2. The other values come from dividing or multiplying the figures wrongly.

items.stem: Which of the following is a longitudinal wave?
options: a sound wave travelling through air
a light wave travelling through a vacuum
a radio wave from a broadcasting station
a ripple spreading on the surface of water
items.explanation: In a sound wave the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of travel, so it is longitudinal. Light and radio waves are transverse electromagnetic waves, and surface ripples are mainly transverse.

items.stem: A current of 2 A flows through a resistor of resistance 5 ohms for 10 seconds. Calculate the heat energy produced in the resistor.
items.explanation: Using the relation heat equals current squared times resistance times time, 4 times 5 times 10 gives 200 J. The alternatives drop one of the squared or time factors.

items.stem: Calculate the pressure at a depth of 5 m in a liquid of density 1000 kg/m^3, taking the acceleration of free fall as 10 m/s^2.
items.explanation: Pressure in a liquid is depth times density times gravity, so 5 times 1000 times 10 gives 50 000 Pa, or 5.0 x 10^4 Pa. The other powers of ten come from misplaced decimal points.

items.stem: Which of the following quantities is a vector?
items.explanation: Force has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector. Mass, speed and energy are scalars because they are completely described by magnitude alone.

items.stem: A body of mass 2 kg moving at 3 m/s collides with and sticks to a stationary body of mass 4 kg. Calculate their common velocity after the collision.
items.explanation: By conservation of momentum, 2 times 3 equals the total mass 6 times the common velocity, giving 1 m/s. The other values arise from adding or ignoring the second mass.

items.stem: The device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy is called
items.explanation: A generator turns mechanical energy into electrical energy. A motor does the reverse, a transformer changes voltage, and a rectifier converts alternating current to direct current.

items.stem: An object is placed 20 cm from a converging lens of focal length 10 cm. Which of the following best describes the image formed?
options: real, inverted and of the same size as the object
items.explanation: The object is at twice the focal length, so the image is formed at twice the focal length on the other side and is real, inverted and the same size. The other descriptions fit different object distances.

items.stem: Which of the following best explains why a metal rod expands when it is heated?
options: The particles melt and flow apart
New particles are created inside the metal
The particles lose electrons to the surroundings
The particles vibrate with greater amplitude about fixed positions
items.explanation: Heating increases the amplitude of vibration of the particles about their fixed positions, so the rod lengthens. The metal does not melt, create new particles, or lose electrons when simply warmed.

items.stem: A force of 20 N acts on a body and moves it through a distance of 3 m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done by the force.
items.explanation: Work done is force times distance when they are in the same direction, so 20 times 3 gives 60 J. The other figures come from adding or dividing the quantities instead of multiplying.

items.stem: The half-life of a radioactive substance is 5 days. What fraction of the original nuclei remains undecayed after 15 days?
items.explanation: Fifteen days is three half-lives, and each half-life halves the remaining nuclei, so one half cubed gives one eighth. The other fractions ignore the doubling of decay per half-life.

items.stem: Which of the following is the correct electronic configuration of a chlorine atom whose atomic number is 17?
items.explanation: Chlorine has 17 electrons, which fill the orbitals to give 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p5. The other configurations account for eighteen, sixteen or fifteen electrons respectively.

items.stem: Which of the following gases is the most abundant in the atmosphere?
items.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about seventy-eight per cent of the atmosphere by volume. Oxygen is next at about twenty-one per cent, while carbon dioxide and argon are present only in small amounts.

items.stem: What is the IUPAC name of the compound with the formula CH3CH2CH2OH?
items.explanation: The compound is a three-carbon alcohol with the hydroxyl group on the end carbon, so it is propan-1-ol. Propan-2-ol has the group in the middle, while propanal and propanoic acid carry different functional groups.

items.stem: Which of the following changes is a chemical change?
options: the rusting of an iron nail
the cutting of a piece of wood
items.explanation: Rusting forms a new substance, hydrated iron oxide, so it is a chemical change. Melting, boiling and cutting only change the physical state or form of the same substance.

items.stem: A solution has a pH of 3. Which of the following best describes the solution?
items.explanation: A pH below 7 shows that a solution is acidic, and a value of 3 is clearly in the acidic range. Neutral is 7, and basic solutions have pH values above 7.

items.stem: Which of the following salts is soluble in water?
items.explanation: All common sodium salts are soluble, so sodium chloride dissolves readily. Silver chloride, barium sulphate and lead(II) sulphate are all well-known insoluble salts.

items.stem: Calculate the number of moles present in 44 g of carbon dioxide, given that its molar mass is 44 g/mol.
items.explanation: The number of moles is mass divided by molar mass, so 44 g divided by 44 g/mol gives 1 mole. The other answers result from multiplying or inverting the calculation.

items.stem: Which of the following elements is a noble gas?
items.explanation: Helium belongs to Group 0, the noble gases, and has a complete outer shell. Hydrogen, nitrogen and chlorine are not noble gases and readily take part in reactions.

items.stem: In the reaction between an acid and a base, the products are
items.explanation: Acid and base react in neutralisation to give a salt and water. Hydrogen gas is produced when acids react with metals, not with bases.

items.stem: Which of the following is an example of a homogeneous mixture?
options: a mixture of sand and water
a mixture of oil and water
a mixture of iron filings and sulphur
a solution of salt in water
items.explanation: A salt solution is uniform throughout, so it is homogeneous. The sand, oil and iron-sulphur mixtures are all heterogeneous because their components remain visibly distinct.

items.stem: The process by which a solid changes directly into a gas without passing through the liquid state is called
items.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas, as when iodine or ammonium chloride is heated. Evaporation is liquid to gas, condensation is gas to liquid, and fusion is solid to liquid.

items.stem: Which of the following is the correct chemical formula for sulphuric acid?
items.explanation: Sulphuric acid is H2SO4, containing two hydrogen atoms and the sulphate ion. HCl is hydrochloric acid, HNO3 is nitric acid, and H2CO3 is carbonic acid.

items.stem: An element has an atomic number of 12. To which group of the periodic table does it belong?
items.explanation: The element is magnesium, with two electrons in its outer shell, so it belongs to group 2. Group 1 has one outer electron, group 3 has three, and group 12 is a transition metal group.

items.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes oxidation?
options: It is the gain of electrons by a substance
It is the loss of oxygen by a substance
It is the gain of hydrogen by a substance
It is the loss of electrons by a substance
items.explanation: Oxidation is the loss of electrons, summarised in the memory aid that oxidation is loss. Gain of electrons is reduction, while the remaining options also describe reduction processes.

items.stem: Which of the following substances will conduct electricity?
options: a solution of sugar in water
items.explanation: Molten sodium chloride contains free-moving ions and so conducts electricity. The solid has ions locked in place, while distilled water and sugar solution contain no free ions.

items.stem: Which of the following organelles is responsible for the synthesis of proteins in a cell?
items.explanation: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis. Mitochondria release energy, lysosomes digest waste, and chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis.

items.stem: The part of the human eye that controls the amount of light entering the eye is the
items.explanation: The iris adjusts the size of the pupil to regulate the light entering the eye. The cornea and lens focus light, while the retina receives the image.

items.stem: Which of the following blood vessels carries oxygenated blood away from the heart?
items.explanation: The aorta carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the body. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs, the vena cava returns deoxygenated blood, and the pulmonary vein returns oxygenated blood to the heart.

items.stem: Photosynthesis in green plants takes place mainly in the
items.explanation: The chloroplast contains chlorophyll and is the site of photosynthesis. Mitochondria are for respiration, the nucleus controls activities, and the vacuole stores materials.

items.stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the stages of mitosis?
items.explanation: Mitosis proceeds through prophase, then metaphase, then anaphase, then telophase. The other sequences reverse or scramble the order of chromosome alignment and separation.

items.stem: The structure that prevents food from entering the windpipe during swallowing is the
items.explanation: The epiglottis closes over the opening of the windpipe as food is swallowed. The larynx is the voice box, the oesophagus carries food to the stomach, and the diaphragm aids breathing.

items.stem: Which of the following organisms is a mammal?
items.explanation: The whale is a mammal because it breathes with lungs, is warm-blooded and suckles its young. The shark and tuna are fish, and the crocodile is a reptile.

items.stem: The exchange of gases in the lungs takes place in the
items.explanation: The alveoli have thin, moist walls and a rich blood supply, making them the site of gaseous exchange. The bronchi and trachea only conduct air, and the diaphragm is a muscle of breathing.

items.stem: A cross is made between two heterozygous tall pea plants, both of genotype Tt. What ratio of tall to short offspring is expected?
items.explanation: A Tt by Tt cross gives genotypes TT, Tt, Tt and tt, so three of the four are tall and one is short. The other ratios do not follow from the monohybrid cross.

items.stem: Which of the following is a function of the kidney in the human body?
options: removal of urea from the blood
items.explanation: The kidney filters the blood and removes urea in urine. Red blood cells are made in bone marrow, digestive enzymes come from glands, and bile is stored in the gall bladder.

items.stem: The green pigment in plants that traps light energy for photosynthesis is
items.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy and is the chief photosynthetic pigment. Haemoglobin carries oxygen in blood, melanin colours skin, and carotene is an accessory pigment.

items.stem: Which of the following organisms acts as a decomposer in an ecosystem?
items.explanation: Fungi break down dead organic matter and return nutrients to the soil, so they are decomposers. The grasshopper and cow are consumers, and the hawk is a predator.

items.stem: The movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane from a region of higher water concentration to a region of lower water concentration is called
items.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water through a semi-permeable membrane down a concentration gradient. Diffusion does not require a membrane, active transport uses energy, and transpiration is water loss from leaves.

items.stem: The digestion of starch begins in the
items.explanation: Salivary amylase in the mouth starts the breakdown of starch into simpler sugars. The stomach acts mainly on proteins, and the intestines complete the digestion of the products.

items.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of all living organisms?
options: they move from place to place
items.explanation: Irritability, or response to stimuli, is shown by every living organism. Locomotion, a backbone and food manufacture are not shared by all living things, since plants and many simple organisms lack them.
